issues_detected.description: Institutional attribution is internally implausible. The principal investigator Aaron Y. Lee is given the affiliation 'Washington University in St. Louis' with ROR:01yc7t268, and the same institution is named as accountable organization and licensor, while every other element of the record places the project at the University of Washington: IRB protocol STUDY00016228 of the 'University of Washington Institutional Review Board, Human Subjects Division' with the hsdrely@uw.edu contact and a Seattle postal address, the NIH RePORTER award organization 'University of Washington', the central laboratory 'University of Washington Nutrition and Obesity Research Center', and the LeeLab Anura sensor 'built ... at the Karalis Johnson Retina Center, University of Washington'. ROR 01yc7t268 denotes Washington University in St. Louis, a distinct institution from the University of Washington. The record discloses the tension in creators.source_caveats and data_governance.source_caveats and resolves it by source tier in favour of the less plausible reading.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record the University of Washington (ROR:00cvxb145) as the PI affiliation and accountable organization, or state explicitly that the FAIRhub 'Washington University in St. Louis' string is a suspected upstream registry error retained verbatim, rather than adopting it as the asserted value.

issues_detected.description: De-identification claims conflict. is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present is false and is_deidentified.method states that 'no identifiers were collected so no active de-identification was necessary' (FAIRhub deIdentType 'NoDeIdentification'), while deidentification_details quotes the public set being 'stripped of Protected Health Information (PHI) ... via the Safe Harbor method', participant_privacy.anonymization_method describes 'Removal of HIPAA-defined Protected Health Information', and preprocessing_strategies lists 'Removal of protected health information, and of sex, race/ethnicity and medication information, from the public release'. A removal step either was or was not applied; the record also notes that the healthsheet question on measures to avoid re-identification was left unanswered.
issues_detected.recommendation: State one operative de-identification determination for the released artifact (Safe Harbor removal applied to the public release) and keep the FAIRhub 'NoDeIdentification' flag as a source note, rather than asserting both as the method.

issues_detected.description: A version that carries its own DOI is declared unavailable. version_access states 'Version 2.0.0 is recorded on FAIRhub and in its documentation as no longer accessible' while also listing 'version 2.0.0, DOI 10.60775/fairhub.2'. A resolvable persistent identifier whose object is withdrawn weakens the persistence claim on which Q13 and Q19 depend. The disclosed notice that 'This repository is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives' is a further, unquantified availability risk.
issues_detected.recommendation: Document the retirement policy for superseded versions (tombstone page, retained metadata, availability on request) and state the preservation commitment and its funding horizon beyond the grant period.

issues_detected.description: Sensitivity flags are more permissive than the surrounding controls. confidential_elements_present and sensitive_elements_present are both false and confidentiality_details asserts the dataset 'does not contain data that might be considered confidential', while the release is nevertheless governed by verified-ID login, a self-attestation access gate, per-licensee static watermarking, storage confined to institutional or BAA-covered infrastructure, and compliance with the NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy security standards, and participant_privacy acknowledges a theoretical re-identification risk.
issues_detected.recommendation: Reconcile the boolean flags with the enforced controls, e.g. by recording that the public release carries residual sensitivity (retinal imaging and continuous physiological traces are potentially re-identifying) even though no direct identifiers are present.

issues_detected.description: No data protection impact analysis exists: data_protection_impacts records only that 'No data protection impact analysis has been conducted for the dataset'. This is an accurate disclosure, but it leaves the acknowledged re-identification risk unassessed for a human-subjects release, and it is the gap that keeps Q8 below the comprehensive band.
issues_detected.recommendation: Conduct and record a data protection impact analysis covering the imaging, waveform and continuous-sensor modalities, which carry re-identification potential that the removal of PHI does not address.

issues_detected.description: Two Q1 slots are unpopulated although equivalent content exists elsewhere: parent_datasets is absent (version predecessors are instead typed in related_datasets as is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 and fairhub.1), and regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is unpopulated although the value 'HL7:2N (normal)' is recorded in regulatory_restrictions.notes. An errata slot is likewise absent, with changes carried in an external CHANGELOG.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate parent_datasets and regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level with the values already present in prose, and add an errata slot summarising the changes that the CHANGELOG records (for example the removal of Snellen acuity variables in 3.0.0).

issues_detected.description: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included is false while special_protections enumerates substantive safeguards (age floor of 40 and ceiling of 85 excluding minors, exclusion of pregnancy, gestational diabetes and type 1 diabetes, capacity to consent, and an incidental-findings pathway for hypertensive crisis, retinal detachment, tumour and optic disc oedema). The flag and its content read in opposite directions, although the reading that no protected class is targeted is defensible.
issues_detected.recommendation: Either set the flag to reflect that a clinically vulnerable adult population with chronic disease is enrolled, or state explicitly that the flag refers to regulatorily protected classes only.

issues_detected.description: subpopulations.source_caveats reports that the healthsheet answers 'No' to whether the dataset identifies demographic sub-populations, while four subpopulation objects with full distributions are serialized. The record reconciles this by noting that sex, race and ethnicity are withheld from the public release and that the counts come from the release README, but the serialized objects do not carry a per-object marker of which distributions are public and which are controlled-access aggregates.
issues_detected.recommendation: Mark each subpopulation object as released or controlled-access-only, so a reuser can tell which variables are actually present in the downloadable files.

issues_detected.description: ip_restrictions quotes the RO-Crate copyright notice 'Copyright (c) 2026 AI-READI' for a release issued 2025-11-17, a forward-dated notice relative to every other date in the record. Quoted faithfully from the source, but temporally anomalous.
issues_detected.recommendation: Note that the copyright year is taken verbatim from the RO-Crate and does not indicate a later release date.

semantic_insights: Arithmetic across the nine file_collections reconciles with the declared totals: the per-collection total_bytes sum to 3,815,969,360,064 against a declared total_size_bytes of 3,815,969,779,678, a difference of 419,614 bytes, and the per-collection file_count values sum to 356,334 against a declared total_file_count of 356,343, a difference of exactly 9 - matching the nine root-level Clinical Dataset Structure metadata files enumerated in notes (CHANGELOG.md, dataset_description.json, dataset_structure_description.json, healthsheet.md, LICENSE.txt, participants.json, participants.tsv, README.md, study_description.json). The source_caveats explanation of the discrepancy is verified by the numbers themselves.

Every demographic table in splits and subpopulations is internally consistent: 1,576 + 352 + 352 = 2,280; race/ethnicity per split (204/369/343/660 training) sums to 1,576 and across splits to the subpopulation totals Hispanic 380, Asian 545, Black 519, White 836; sex sums to male 951 and female 1,329; diabetes status sums to 776/560/686/258. All four marginals equal the declared instance count of 2,280.

Temporal ordering is coherent: IRB initial approval 2022-12-20 precedes the collection window 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01, which precedes the 2025-11-17 issue date; releases are ordered 1.0.0 (2024-05-03), 2.0.0 (2024-11-08), 3.0.0 (2025-11-17); the NIH award period 2022-09-01 to 2025-08-31 brackets the collection window.

Identifier formats validate: the dataset DOI prefix 10.60775 is a DataCite prefix consistent with the FAIRhub landing page at fairhub.io/datasets/3; the license DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17555036 uses the Zenodo prefix; the associated publication DOIs 10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x and 10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449 use the Springer Nature and BMJ prefixes and match the journals named in prose; subcrate identifiers use well-formed ARK strings (ark:59853/rocrate-b2ai-ai-readi-*); NCT06002048 is a well-formed ClinicalTrials.gov identifier.

All four grant numbers follow NIH activity-code conventions and are semantically plausible for the claims made: OT2OD032644 is an Other Transaction award through the Office of the Director, the mechanism used by the Common Fund Bridge2AI program, and the record supplies the matching RePORTER application ID 10471118, project number 1OT2OD032644-01 and award amount; P30DK035816 is an NIDDK centre grant and UL1TR003096 an NCATS CTSA award, both appropriate supporting mechanisms.

Standards claims are specific and modality-appropriate rather than decorative: OMOP CDM for tabular clinical data with each CSV mapping one-to-one to a CDM table and a dqd_omop.json quality file, DICOM for all seven retinal imaging devices with the .fda and .sdt native exports named as converted inputs, WFDB for the 12-lead ECG whose native export is Philips XML, Open mHealth for Garmin .FIT and Dexcom traces, and the NASA Earth-science ASCII guidelines for the environmental sensor - each standard is attached to the modality it actually governs.

The dataset-level de-identification posture is coherent with the AI/ML reuse framing: withholding sex, race/ethnicity and medications from the public release while shipping a validation/test split balanced on exactly those withheld variables is an unusual but internally consistent design, and future_use_impacts names the resulting auditability limitation rather than concealing it.

Bias documentation uses schema enumeration terms (selection_bias, sampling_bias, representation_bias) and ties each to a concrete recruitment fact - volunteer enrolment, ICD-10 screening of three academic health systems, and deliberate equal-proportion recruitment of four race/ethnic groups - with mitigation strategies attached to two of the three.

questions.name: Field Completeness
questions.description: Proportion of mandatory schema fields populated (id, title, description, keywords, license).
questions.score_label: Approximately 86% of the named fields populated - very good, short of the 90% band
questions.evidence: Populated: id 'doi:10.60775/fairhub.3'; title 'Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project'; description (~2,000 characters); keywords (10 terms); license_and_use_terms (license_terms plus data_use_permission 'disease_specific_research'); doi '10.60775/fairhub.3'; page 'https://fairhub.io/datasets/3'; creators (consortium plus PI with ROR and ORCID); purposes (4 responses); instances (1 object, counts 2280); variables (25 objects with data_type, unit, measurement_technique); external_resources (6 entries, read here as the 'resources' requirement). Unpopulated: parent_datasets (version predecessors carried instead in related_datasets as is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 and doi:10.60775/fairhub.1); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level (value 'HL7:2N (normal)' present only in regulatory_restrictions.notes).
questions.quality_note: Twelve of fourteen named fields are populated with substantive content, and the two gaps have prose equivalents elsewhere in the record rather than being genuinely undocumented. On a field-presence count that is 85.7%, below the 90% threshold the 5 band requires, so 4.
questions.semantic_analysis: Field content is semantically appropriate to each slot rather than padded: variables carry units and measurement techniques, instances carries a real count and a labelling rationale, and the id/doi/page triple resolves consistently to the same FAIRhub object. The two unpopulated slots are recorded gaps rather than missing information, which is why this scores at the top of the 'minor gaps' band.

questions.name: Entry Length Adequacy
questions.description: Whether narrative fields (description, purposes) have meaningful content length.
questions.score_label: >200 chars
questions.evidence: description runs approximately 2,000 characters and names the cohort size (2,280), the collection window (19 July 2023 to 1 May 2025), the three sites, the four diabetes categories, more than ten data domains, the file and byte totals (356,343 files, ~3.82 TB) and the governing standards. purposes contains four responses each of 200-400 characters, e.g. 'To develop a foundational dataset in T2DM that is agnostic to existing classification criteria or biases and that can be used to reconstruct a temporal atlas of T2DM development and reversal towards health.'
questions.quality_note: Both narrative fields are far above the >200 character band and, more importantly, the length is carrying specifics rather than boilerplate.
questions.semantic_analysis: Every quantity asserted in the description is corroborated elsewhere in the record (2,280 matches instances.counts and all four demographic marginals; 356,343 matches total_file_count; the date range matches collection_timeframes), so the narrative is not merely long but verifiable against the structured fields.

questions.name: Keyword Diversity
questions.description: Number of unique keywords provided to describe dataset topic coverage.
questions.score_label: >=8 keywords
questions.evidence: 10 unique keywords: 'Diabetes mellitus', 'Machine Learning', 'Artificial Intelligence', 'Electrocardiography', 'Continuous Glucose Monitoring', 'Retinal imaging', 'Eye exam', 'Type 2 Diabetes', 'Data Sharing', 'Exploratory Data Collection'.
questions.quality_note: Ten distinct terms, meeting the >=8 band.
questions.semantic_analysis: The keyword set spans disease, method and modality axes and each term is discharged by actual content: Electrocardiography by the cardiac_ecg subcrate, Continuous Glucose Monitoring by the Dexcom G6 collection, Retinal imaging by four imaging subcrates. 'Diabetes mellitus' and 'Type 2 Diabetes' partly overlap, and the environmental-sensor and wearable-activity modalities - two of the more distinctive parts of the release - have no keyword of their own.

questions.name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
questions.description: Number of distribution formats and file type diversity.
questions.score_label: >3 file types
questions.evidence: distribution_formats lists four typed entries - application/dicom, text/csv, application/json, text/markdown - each with an access URL, and the notes add 'tab-separated manifest.tsv files for each data type and a participants.tsv file at the root'. total_file_count 356343; nine file_collections enumerate per-collection file_count and total_bytes (e.g. retinal_octa 173,721 files / 1,155,908,809,724 bytes; cardiac_ecg 4,515 files / 302,931,703 bytes).
questions.quality_note: Five distinct media types with per-collection enumeration, comfortably above the >3 band.
questions.semantic_analysis: Format variety genuinely reflects the multi-modal claim in description and keywords rather than incidental packaging: DICOM for the five imaging subcrates, CSV for OMOP clinical tables, JSON for Open mHealth wearable records and the CDS metadata files, TSV for manifests and the participant split. The TSV format is described only in a note rather than given its own distribution_formats entry.

questions.name: Data File Size Availability
questions.description: Presence of file size or instance count metadata.
questions.score_label: Pass
questions.evidence: total_size_bytes: 3815969779678; total_file_count: 356343; instances.counts: 2280; nine file_collections each with total_bytes and file_count; splits give 1,576 / 352 / 352; version_access records that 'Version 2.0.0 comprised 165,051 files and 2.01 TB; version 3.0.0 comprises 356,343 files and 3.82 TB'.
questions.quality_note: Numeric size and instance metadata are present at dataset, collection and version level - well beyond the pass threshold.
questions.semantic_analysis: Size metadata is not merely present but checkable: the nine collection byte totals sum to within 419,614 bytes of the declared total, the residual matching the nine root metadata files, and the file counts differ by exactly 9 for the same reason.

questions.name: Dataset Identification Metadata
questions.description: Presence of unique identifiers such as DOI, RRID, or persistent URLs.
questions.score_label: Pass
questions.evidence: doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3; id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; publisher: https://fairhub.io/; version_access.latest_version_doi doi:10.60775/fairhub.3 with per-version DOIs 10.60775/fairhub.1 and .2; nine ARK identifiers of the form ark:59853/rocrate-b2ai-ai-readi-omop; ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648 for the PI; ROR:01yc7t268 for the affiliation.
questions.quality_note: Multiple persistent identifiers at dataset, version, subcrate and person level.
questions.semantic_analysis: Identifiers are internally coherent - id, doi and latest_version_doi agree, and the page URL path (/datasets/3) matches the DOI suffix (fairhub.3). No RRID is asserted, which is consistent with the record's stated practice of not asserting identifiers no source supplies. The ROR is well formed but points at the institution this evaluation flags as a probable attribution error.

questions.name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
questions.description: Presence of funding sources, grants, creator affiliations, and institutional sponsors.
questions.score_label: Funders with grants + creators with affiliations
questions.evidence: funders: National Institutes of Health with grants OT2OD032644 ('Awarded through the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program ... application ID 10471118, project number 1OT2OD032644-01, an award amount of $5,026,499 for fiscal year 2022 ... project period of 1 September 2022 to 31 August 2025'), P30DK035816, UL1TR003096, plus Research to Prevent Blindness. creators: 'AI-READI Consortium' (organizational) and principal_investigator 'Aaron Y. Lee' with affiliation id ROR:01yc7t268 and ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648 in notes. notes additionally acknowledges in-kind device support from Topcon, Optomed, iCare, Zeiss, Heidelberg, Dexcom and Garmin and cloud support from the Microsoft AI for Good Lab.
questions.quality_note: Four funders, three grant numbers, an award amount, a project period and a RePORTER application ID, together with creator affiliations and an ORCID - the top band with room to spare.
questions.semantic_analysis: Grant formats validate against NIH conventions and the activity codes are plausible for the claims made (OT2/OD for a Common Fund Other Transaction, P30/DK for a NIDDK centre, UL1/TR for a CTSA). The one semantic defect is the affiliation: the RePORTER organization is recorded as University of Washington in the same funders.notes that sits beside a creators affiliation of Washington University in St. Louis. Because the funding content itself is complete and the conflict is disclosed in source_caveats, it is logged as an issue rather than scored down here; it is scored where it bears on governance attribution.

questions.name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
questions.applicability_evidence: Human-subject condition met on non-Q8 fields: description (Q1-Q2) states 'A multimodal, AI-ready dataset of 2,280 adult participants with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus'; keywords (Q3) include 'Type 2 Diabetes' and 'Eye exam'; collection_mechanisms (Q12) describe recruitment and in-person participant procedures ('REDCap ... hosted the recruitment interface and electronic consent'; 'Blood pressure and heart rate measured twice ... with an automatic oscillometric medically approved device').
questions.description: Comprehensive ethics coverage including IRB approval, deidentification, privacy protections, informed consent, participant compensation, and vulnerable population safeguards.
questions.score_label: Very comprehensive human-subject protections; data protection impact analysis absent
questions.evidence: ethical_reviews: 'University of Washington Institutional Review Board, Human Subjects Division ... protocol number STUDY00016228, with initial approval on 20 December 2022 and reliance agreements with the IRBs of the University of Alabama at Birmingham and the University of California, San Diego', plus a second review entry naming four named bioethicists and an eleven-person Community Advisory Board. human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects true with irb_approval, ethics_review_board contact (hsdrely@uw.edu, postal address), regulatory_compliance and special_populations. is_deidentified with method, identifiers_removed and deidentification_details. participant_privacy with anonymization_method, privacy_techniques (verified-ID login, strict license, static watermarking), reidentification_risk and data_linkage. informed_consent: consent_obtained true, written/electronic consent type, consent_scope, consent_documentation ('AI-READI Consent_Form_Standard_Mod17May2023_useforpilot.pdf') and withdrawal_mechanism; collection_consents, collection_notifications and consent_revocations add further detail. participant_compensation: US$200 stipend, payment conditions, plus transport reimbursement. at_risk_populations.special_protections covers the 40-85 age window, exclusion of pregnancy/gestational/type 1 diabetes, and an incidental-findings pathway. regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance covers HIPAA and the NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy. Against this: data_protection_impacts states only 'No data protection impact analysis has been conducted for the dataset'; no hipaa_compliant term is asserted; no governance committee contact person is named (data_governance.source_caveats: 'No contact person is asserted for the governance committee').
questions.quality_note: Among the most complete ethics documentation the rubric contemplates - protocol number, approval date, reliance agreements, consent artefact filename, withdrawal terms, exact compensation and its conditions. It falls one band short because the 5 requires data protection impacts to be documented and the record documents that no such analysis exists, leaving the acknowledged re-identification risk unassessed.
questions.semantic_analysis: Cross-field logic holds where it matters: involves_human_subjects true is matched by populated ethical_reviews and informed_consent, and is_deidentified is matched by a stated method and by participant_privacy protections. Two semantic defects reduce confidence rather than coverage - the NoDeIdentification / Safe Harbor conflict in is_deidentified, and sensitivity flags set to false beneath an access regime (watermarking, BAA-only storage, GDS security standards) whose restrictiveness implies residual sensitivity. The ethics claims are otherwise plausible for the data type: withholding sex, race/ethnicity and medications is a stronger-than-Safe-Harbor step and is justified on stigmatization grounds.

questions.name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
questions.description: Whether access policy, license, IP restrictions, regulatory restrictions, and confidentiality level are clearly defined.
questions.score_label: License + restrictions + confidentiality classification
questions.evidence: license_and_use_terms: 'AI-READI Data License Agreement version 2.0, published at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036', with grant scope (non-exclusive, non-transferable, research/commercial/non-commercial, derivative works permitted), sublicensing rules, automatic termination on breach, attribution duty, as-is warranty disclaimer and a one-dollar liability cap; data_use_permission 'disease_specific_research'. ip_restrictions: title and all IP remain with the licensor, reserved rights, indemnity, the RO-Crate copyright notice, and referral of large-scale reproduction requests. regulatory_restrictions: compliance with applicable law, other_compliance covering the NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy Best Practices and the HIPAA position, notes recording confidentialityLevel 'HL7:2N (normal)'. data_governance: committee name, accountable organization, access_review_process ('logging in through a verified ID system; agreeing to use the data only for type 2 diabetes related research; and agreeing to the license terms ... FAIRhub access type ... PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired') and a separate controlled-access route via legal and privacy use agreements.
questions.quality_note: All three elements of the top band are present, and the access review process distinguishes the public and controlled tiers with their respective requirements.
questions.semantic_analysis: Governance and licence terms are mutually consistent and proportionate to the claimed sensitivity: disease-specific permission matches the intended_uses restriction to type 2 diabetes research, the prohibition on third-party model-vendor sharing matches the watermarking rationale in participant_privacy, and the controlled-access tier holds exactly the elements sensitive_elements lists as withheld. The confidentiality classification is asserted only in a notes string rather than in the confidentiality_level slot, and no HIPAA compliance determination is asserted - both disclosed, and neither leaves the reuser without the substance.

questions.name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
questions.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met on non-Q10 fields: distribution_formats (Q4) lists four media types each with access_urls 'https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access'; page (Q6/Q16) resolves to the FAIRhub landing page; license_and_use_terms (Q9/Q18) grants 'a non-exclusive, non-transferable license to download, reproduce and use the data'.
questions.description: Presence of standard formats, ontologies, schema conformance, cross-platform dataset linkages with typed relationships, and dataset integration capability.
questions.score_label: Standard formats + schema/ontology compliance + integration capability
questions.evidence: conforms_to 'Clinical Dataset Structure (CDS) v0.1.1' with the specification URL in external_resources; conforms_to_standard [CDS, DICOM, OMOP_CDM, WFDB, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS]; conforms_to_schema 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema' with conforms_to_class 'Dataset'; each of the nine file_collections carries its own conforms_to and conforms_to_standard (e.g. cardiac_ecg -> WFDB + CDS; clinical_data -> OMOP_CDM + CDS with 'each CSV file in this directory is a one-to-one mapping to an OMOP CDM table' and a dqd_omop.json quality file). Integration: relationships records that 'files from different data types, modalities and devices are related by the participant identifier, which names the participant-level folder under every device folder'; preprocessing_strategies records RxNorm coding of medications; related_datasets carries typed links (is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 and .1; is_documented_by doi:10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x and doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449).
questions.quality_note: Six standards, each bound to the modality it governs, plus LinkML schema conformance, a documented cross-modality join key and typed cross-dataset relationships - the full top band.
questions.semantic_analysis: The standards claims survive semantic checking rather than reading as a badge list: the native export format is named for each converted modality (.fda and .sdt to DICOM, Philips XML to WFDB, Garmin .FIT to Open mHealth), so a reuser can tell what conversion was performed. Integration capability is real - one participant identifier joins survey, clinical, imaging, waveform, wearable and environmental records - though harmonisation across the seven retinal devices is acknowledged in known_limitations as introducing between-device variation the user must handle. No ontology term identifiers (for example AIO or MeSH CURIEs) are attached to keywords or bias types, which is the one standardization axis left in prose.

questions.name: Tool and Software Transparency
questions.applicability_evidence: Software-output condition met on a non-Q11 field: external_resources (Q14) references a code repository - 'GitHub organization of the AI-READI project at https://github.com/AI-READI' - and also a Zenodo community and the CDS specification repository. Scored rather than excluded on that evidence, per the anti-circular rule.
questions.description: Mentions of preprocessing, cleaning, and labeling strategies with software tools used in data preparation, including annotation quality, imputation, and missing data documentation.
questions.score_label: Comprehensive strategies; software names and versions only partly supplied
questions.evidence: preprocessing_strategies (7 entries): OMOP CDM mapping with RxNorm medication coding; DICOM conversion naming which devices export DICOM natively and which are converted from .fda and .sdt; Open mHealth conversion of Garmin .FIT; WFDB conversion of Philips XML and ESDS for the environmental sensor; CDS v0.1.1 directory organization with manifest.tsv per data type; static watermarking; PHI and demographic removal. cleaning_strategies (3 entries): REDCap range flagging with coordinator and data-manager review, credibility/skip-pattern/missing/duplicate checks, edits only under site PI approval; internal PII review with 'The dataset has not undergone any formal external audits'; 'dqd_omop.json, supporting the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard, which runs a set of more than 3,500 data quality checks'. missing_data_documentation supplies patterns, causes and handling_strategy ('Missing values are not imputed'). Labeling: instances.label false with 'No labeling was performed, because the dataset is hypothesis agnostic'. Absent: machine_annotation_tools, annotation_analyses, and any named conversion software with a version or repository URL.
questions.quality_note: Strategy documentation is comprehensive and the quality-control workflow is specific down to who may authorise an edit. It stops short of the top band because the tooling itself is largely unnamed: REDCap, the MoCA Duo application and the OMOP Data Quality Dashboard appear without versions, and no software or repository is identified for the .fda/.sdt-to-DICOM, XML-to-WFDB or .FIT-to-Open-mHealth conversions that the release depends on.
questions.semantic_analysis: The absence of labeling and imputation is a documented design decision consistent with the hypothesis-agnostic framing in purposes and other_tasks, not an omission, and is credited as such. The GitHub organization is referenced but not tied to any named pipeline, so a reuser cannot reproduce the conversions from this record alone - the gap that separates 4 from 5 here.

questions.name: Collection Protocol Clarity
questions.applicability_evidence: Collection-and-sharing condition met: collection fields are populated (acquisition_methods, collection_mechanisms, data_collectors, collection_timeframes) and the datasets-shared condition is met on non-Q12 fields - distribution_formats (Q4) with access_urls and license_and_use_terms (Q9) permitting download and reuse.
questions.description: Description completeness of data collection mechanisms, acquisition methods, data collectors, and collection timeframes.
questions.score_label: Full collection protocol with methods, collectors, and timeframes
questions.evidence: acquisition_methods: directly observed, subject-reported and validated flags all true, with verification 'by cross-referencing entered medications against medications that were physically brought in or photographed by each study participant'. collection_mechanisms: eleven entries naming device make, model and protocol - REDCap EDC; Philips PageWriter TC30 with chair angle recorded as 0/30/60/90 degrees; Dexcom G6 sampling every five minutes over ten days with participants masked; Garmin Vivosmart 5 at five-second intervals with wrist and handedness recorded; LeeLab Anura with its sensor list and explicit absence of video, audio and GPS; seven named retinal imaging systems; MoCA Duo on iPad; three named blood-pressure devices measured twice two minutes apart; M&S EVA at four metres with a 2.0 neutral density filter for mesopic testing; 10 g monofilament at three plantar locations ten times each; ~53 mL non-fasting blood draw with local CBC and central batch assay. data_collectors: six roles with training and certification requirements ('mandatory institutional compliance training for human subject research and successful administration of all protocol elements to at least three volunteer practice subjects'). collection_timeframes: start_date 2023-07-19, end_date 2025-05-01, with pilot and formal phases distinguished. raw_data_sources: eight entries with source_type and native format. sampling_strategies: non-probability wave-based recruitment with ICD-10 screening codes E11.X and R73.09.
questions.quality_note: Protocol documentation is at the level of a manual of procedures: instrument, setting, timing, operator qualification and verification step are all recoverable. Comfortably the top band.
questions.semantic_analysis: Collection detail is consistent with every downstream claim: the ten-day concurrent wear of CGM, activity tracker and home sensor explains the per-collection file counts (2,246 CGM, 2,232 environment, 15,245 wearable); the device list matches the imaging subcrates one for one; the single-visit design matches the cross-sectional limitation in known_limitations and the absence of longitudinal linkage in relationships. The FAIRhub versus BMJ Open start-date discrepancy (19 versus 18 July 2023) is one day and is disclosed with its resolution.

questions.name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
questions.applicability_evidence: Collection-and-sharing condition met on non-Q13 fields: collection_timeframes and collection_mechanisms (Q12) are populated, and distribution_formats with access_urls plus a reuse-permitting license (Q4, Q9) establish that the datasets are shared.
questions.description: Presence of version information, version access methods, errata, update plans, release notes with dates, and data sustainability indicators.
questions.score_label: Comprehensive versioning and governance; preservation commitment incomplete
questions.evidence: version '3.0.0'; version_access with latest_version_doi and all three versions with their DOIs and release dates (1.0.0 / 10.60775/fairhub.1 / 3 May 2024; 2.0.0 / .2 / 8 November 2024; 3.0.0 / .3 / 17 November 2025), per-version documentation via a version dropdown, and per-version scale (2.0.0: 165,051 files, 2.01 TB; 3.0.0: 356,343 files, 3.82 TB). updates: frequency 'Approximately once a year', static versions never updated in place, participant counts per version (204 / 1,067 / 2,280), changes recorded in a CHANGELOG. distribution_dates gives the three release dates. maintainers: 'The AI-READI team supports and maintains the dataset. It is hosted on FAIRhub through Microsoft Azure', with contact routes. Repository and persistent ID: FAIRhub with a DOI per version; ARK identifiers per subcrate. retention_limit: 'There are no limits on the retention of the data'. Against this: no errata slot; raw_sources commits to preservation only 'at least for the duration of the project'; version_access states 'Version 2.0.0 is recorded on FAIRhub and in its documentation as no longer accessible'; notes records 'This repository is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives'.
questions.quality_note: Versioning is exemplary - three DOIs, dated releases, per-version scale and documentation, and an explicit immutability policy. Sustainability is the weaker half: governance and a domain-appropriate repository are documented, but the institutional preservation commitment is bounded by the project period, a DOI-bearing prior version is already inaccessible, and the disclosed repository review notice is an unaddressed continuity risk. That combination is a clear 4 rather than the full sustainability band.
questions.semantic_analysis: Version metadata is internally consistent - participant counts across versions (204, 1,067, 2,280) rise monotonically and the 3.0.0 count matches instances.counts and every demographic marginal. The persistence defect is genuine rather than formal: a citable DOI whose object is withdrawn breaks the guarantee that the DOI is meant to carry, and the record surfaces it without describing a tombstone or retrieval-on-request path.

questions.name: Associated Publications
questions.description: Presence of formal citations or external resources with DOI-linked references.
questions.score_label: Two or more distinct references plus a formal dataset citation
questions.evidence: Formal dataset citation identifying title, authors, version, publisher and DOI: 'AI-READI Consortium. (2025). Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project (3.0.0) [Data set]. FAIRhub. https://doi.org/10.60775/fairhub.3'. Distinct further references: related_datasets doi:10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x and doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449, both typed is_documented_by; external_resources entries for https://docs.aireadi.org/, https://aireadi.org/, https://github.com/AI-READI, https://zenodo.org/communities/aireadi, the CDS specification at https://cds-specification.readthedocs.io/en/v0.1.1/, and ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06002048.
questions.quality_note: Well past the two-reference threshold, with a formal citation present, so the top band applies.
questions.semantic_analysis: The publication DOIs are semantically appropriate to their asserted roles - the BMJ Open item is described as the study protocol and the Nature Metabolism item as a comment, and both are cited elsewhere in the record for specific facts (funding statement, Safe Harbor description), so the references are load-bearing rather than ornamental. The record also flags that the BMJ Open paper misreports the ClinicalTrials.gov number as the IRB protocol string, a correctness catch in the source rather than in this datasheet.

questions.name: Human Subject Representation
questions.applicability_evidence: Human-subject condition met on non-Q15 fields: description (Q1-Q2) '2,280 adult participants with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus'; keywords (Q3) 'Type 2 Diabetes'; collection_mechanisms (Q12) describe in-person participant procedures and REDCap-hosted recruitment and consent.
questions.description: Inclusion of human subjects, demographic diversity, or subgroup details.
questions.score_label: Detailed demographics and inclusion/exclusion criteria
questions.evidence: instances: 2,280 participants, each instance spanning survey, clinical, imaging, waveform, wearable and environmental data. subpopulations: four objects with full distributions - race/ethnicity (Hispanic 380, Asian 545, Black 519, White 836), sex (male 951, female 1,329), diabetes status (no diabetes 776, lifestyle 560, oral 686, insulin 258) and age (mean 60.8 +/- 11.3, eligibility 40-85). splits: per-partition demographic tables with means by partition. Inclusion/exclusion: age 40 and over with an 85 ceiling, English speaking, capacity to consent; exclusions pregnancy, gestational diabetes, type 1 diabetes. known_limitations names the absence of Pacific Islanders and Native Americans, the urban hospital-based recruitment base and the English-language requirement. missing_data_documentation explains modality-level non-coverage.
questions.quality_note: Demographic characterisation is quantitative at both cohort and partition level and is paired with explicit eligibility criteria and named coverage gaps - the top band without reservation.
questions.semantic_analysis: All demographic marginals reconcile to 2,280 and to the split tables, so the representation claims are arithmetically sound. A substantive caveat the record itself raises: sex and race/ethnicity are withheld from the public release, so these distributions describe the cohort rather than variables a public reuser can access - which is why future_use_impacts concedes that models built on the public set cannot be audited directly for disparity across those groups. The documentation earns full marks; the dataset's own auditability limit is recorded under Q20 and in the issues list.

questions.name: Findability (Persistent Links)
questions.description: Dataset includes persistent URLs for access and documentation.
questions.score_label: Pass
questions.evidence: page 'https://fairhub.io/datasets/3'; doi '10.60775/fairhub.3'; distribution_formats access_urls 'https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access'; external_resources 'https://docs.aireadi.org/', 'https://aireadi.org/', 'https://github.com/AI-READI', 'https://zenodo.org/communities/aireadi', 'https://cds-specification.readthedocs.io/en/v0.1.1/', 'https://classic.clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT06002048'; license at 'https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036'.
questions.quality_note: Numerous well-formed persistent links across landing page, documentation, code, license and registration.
questions.semantic_analysis: Domains are plausible and consistent with the claimed publisher and program - fairhub.io for the release, zenodo.org for the license deposit, clinicaltrials.gov for the registration - and the DOI suffix matches the landing-page path. Link resolution was not exercised in this offline evaluation; the judgement is on structure and internal consistency.

questions.name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
questions.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met on non-Q17 fields: file_collections and total_file_count (Q4/Q5) enumerate released content, page (Q6/Q16) gives the landing page, and third_party_sharing.is_shared is true with 'The dataset is distributed for public use through the FAIRhub platform'.
questions.description: Describes how users can obtain the dataset (download, DUA, login).
questions.score_label: Fully defined access path (platform, login, policy)
questions.evidence: data_governance.access_review_process: 'logging in through a verified ID system; agreeing to use the data only for type 2 diabetes related research; and agreeing to the license terms ... The FAIRhub access type is recorded as PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired', with the controlled-access tier requiring 'legal and privacy use agreements with the AI-READI research programme'. distribution_formats: four media types each with access_urls 'https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access' and the note 'All data files are in formats accessible with free software commonly used for such data types, so no specific software is required'. license_and_use_terms sets the terms a requester attests to. external_resources notes the version 3.0.0 documentation covers 'preliminary information on access and training prerequisites, the mini-subset version and Azure Storage access'; notes records a 'mini' version for pipeline development.
questions.quality_note: Platform, authentication, attestation, licence gate, format accessibility, bulk-transfer route and a development-scale subset are all specified, and the public and controlled tiers are distinguished - the full band.
questions.semantic_analysis: The access path is consistent with the licence and with the sensitivity posture: self-attestation to disease-specific use matches data_use_permission 'disease_specific_research', and the controlled tier holds exactly the elements sensitive_elements lists as withheld. No download_url slot is populated, but per-format access_urls and the Azure Storage route make the obtaining path concrete. The only unquantified access risk is the disclosed 'under review for potential modification' notice on the repository.

questions.name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
questions.description: License is clearly defined with explicit use guidance including intended uses, prohibited uses, discouraged uses, and comprehensive social impact analysis with risk identification and mitigation strategies.
questions.score_label: License + comprehensive use guidance + social impact analysis with mitigation strategies
questions.evidence: license_and_use_terms with a licence DOI and full grant and termination terms. intended_uses: three use_category objects with examples and usage_notes, including the model-dissemination condition to 'undertake all reasonable efforts to minimize the likelihood that data can be memorized, derived, reconstructed or reconstituted'. prohibited_uses: seven distinct prohibitions - clinical treatment decisions, any re-identification or group-membership inference, sharing with third-party model vendors for training even under a BAA, onward transfer to non-licensees, republication beyond five illustrative figures per paper, watermark removal, and storage outside institutional or BAA-covered infrastructure. future_use_impacts: two entries covering the theoretical re-identification risk with mitigations (dissemination system, strict licence, watermarking) and the fairness consequence of withholding sex and race/ethnicity, mitigated by a validation/test split balanced on those variables 'stated as aimed at reducing disparities in models developed using this dataset'.
questions.quality_note: Use guidance is unusually operational - the prohibitions name the specific reuse behaviours that matter for AI/ML, and the social impact entry pairs an identified harm with a concrete, checkable mitigation. Top band.
questions.semantic_analysis: Permissions and prohibitions are mutually coherent (models may be built and distributed, the data inside them may not travel; derivative and synthetic data inherit the restrictions), and the prohibitions align with the re-identification risk acknowledged in participant_privacy rather than exceeding or falling short of it. No discouraged_uses slot is populated - the record draws a binary permitted/prohibited line with no intermediate cautions - and the first impact entry's claim that the creators 'do not currently anticipate any uses that could result in unfair treatment or harm' is weaker than the analysis in the second entry. Neither is enough to drop a band given the depth elsewhere.

questions.name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
questions.description: Presence of version access, errata, update plans, source derivation, parent dataset linkages, missing data documentation, data split indicators, and provenance graph representation.
questions.score_label: Full lineage in text form: entities, activities, agents and derivation paths
questions.evidence: Entities and derivation paths: raw_data_sources gives eight native sources with formats and their fate - Philips XML 'released as WFDB after conversion', Topcon .fda and Heidelberg .sdt 'Converted to DICOM for the dataset', Garmin .FIT 'Converted to the Open mHealth standard', REDCap exports, central laboratory CSV. Activities: preprocessing_strategies enumerates the mapping, conversion, organization, watermarking and PHI-removal steps; cleaning_strategies enumerates range flagging, credibility and skip-pattern checks, and OMOP DQD analysis. Agents: data_collectors names six roles with responsibilities, site data managers perform 'quality control of all data before uploading to FAIRhub', and edits are made 'only under the guidance and approval of the site principal investigator'. Dataset lineage: related_datasets is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 and .1; version_access and updates document what each version contains. Quality and completeness: missing_data_documentation (patterns, causes, handling), anomalies (six device- and participant-level failure modes), splits, and raw_sources on the retention and non-release of raw data.
questions.quality_note: This is lineage rather than a changelog: for every modality one can trace native export to conversion activity to released standard, name the agent responsible at each stage, and see the quality checks applied. The rubric accepts text-form provenance with complete lineage, which this meets.
questions.semantic_analysis: The provenance is auditable against itself - the conversion targets named in raw_data_sources match the conforms_to_standard values of the corresponding file_collections in every case. Two integrity gaps keep this from being unimprovable rather than from being a 5: there are no file-level checksums or fixity information anywhere in the record, and no was_derived_from or errata slot is populated, so the version lineage and the derivation paths are expressed in prose and in related_datasets rather than as machine-actionable PROV relations. The inaccessibility of version 2.0.0 also breaks the retrievability of one node in that lineage.

questions.name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
questions.description: Metadata documents known biases using standardized taxonomies (BiasTypeEnum, AIO) aligned with CROISSANT RAI standards, and includes fairness analysis.
questions.score_label: Taxonomy-typed biases with fairness analysis; no ontology mappings and one bias unmitigated
questions.evidence: known_biases: three objects typed with enumeration terms - selection_bias ('Participants are volunteers, so there is selection bias known as volunteer bias'), sampling_bias (ICD-10 screening of three academic health systems as the study base, with a mitigation_strategy of uniform protocols and site selection), representation_bias (deliberate equal-proportion recruitment of four race/ethnic groups, exclusion of Pacific Islanders and Native Americans, documented difficulty recruiting Black men, with a mitigation_strategy of wave-based monitoring and under/oversampling). future_use_impacts supplies the fairness analysis: the public release omits sex and race/ethnicity so 'models developed on it cannot be audited directly for disparity across those groups', mitigated by balanced validation and test partitions. known_limitations adds representativeness, coverage, temporal, scope and methodological limitation types, including between-device variation across the seven imaging systems.
questions.quality_note: Bias types use standard enumeration terms, each is grounded in a specific recruitment or measurement fact, and a real fairness analysis with a concrete mitigation is present. It falls short of the top band because no AIO or CROISSANT RAI ontology identifiers are attached to the bias types, the selection_bias entry carries no mitigation_strategy, and no measurement or device bias is typed despite known_limitations describing between-device variation as a methodological limitation.
questions.semantic_analysis: The bias entries are consistent with the sampling and limitation fields rather than generic - sampling_bias matches the ICD-10 codes E11.X and R73.09 in sampling_strategies, and representation_bias matches the four-group balanced design and the named excluded groups. The most consequential fairness issue is stated plainly rather than buried: balancing on sex and race/ethnicity while withholding those variables from the public release means the balance cannot be verified by public reusers, and the record concedes this. Bias is described in prose only; no quantitative fairness metric or per-subgroup performance baseline is supplied.

strengths: Structured content is arithmetically self-consistent to an unusual degree: per-collection byte and file totals reconcile with the declared dataset totals down to the nine root metadata files, and every demographic marginal in subpopulations and splits sums exactly to the 2,280 declared instances.

Collection protocol documentation reaches manual-of-procedures depth - eleven named instruments with make, model, protocol, timing and operator qualification, six collector roles with certification requirements, and an explicit verification step for medication entry.

Ethics and governance are documented end to end: IRB protocol STUDY00016228 with approval date and reliance agreements, the consent artefact by filename, withdrawal terms, exact compensation and its payment conditions, a two-tier access regime, and a licence with operational AI/ML reuse constraints.

Standards conformance is bound to the modality it governs - OMOP CDM, DICOM, WFDB, Open mHealth and the Earth-science ASCII guidelines under a CDS v0.1.1 layout - with each converted modality's native export format named, and LinkML schema conformance declared at the dataset level.

Source conflicts are disclosed rather than smoothed over: the record carries explicit source_caveats for institutional attribution, the de-identification determination, the collection start date, enrolment targets and the acronym expansion, each with the resolution rule applied.

Provenance is traceable in text for every modality, from device-native export through named conversion and quality-control activities to the released standard, with the responsible agent identified at each stage.
weaknesses: Institutional attribution is probably wrong: the PI and accountable organization are recorded as Washington University in St. Louis (ROR:01yc7t268) while the IRB, the NIH award organization, the central laboratory and the sensor development site are all the University of Washington.
The de-identification determination is self-contradictory - 'no active de-identification was necessary' sits alongside a Safe Harbor PHI-stripping description and a PHI-removal preprocessing step.
No data protection impact analysis exists, despite an acknowledged theoretical re-identification risk over imaging and continuous physiological data.

Sustainability is bounded: preservation is committed only 'for the duration of the project', version 2.0.0 is already inaccessible despite holding DOI 10.60775/fairhub.2, and the repository carries an undischarged 'under review for potential modification' notice.
Data-preparation tooling is largely unnamed - no software, version or repository is given for the .fda/.sdt-to-DICOM, XML-to-WFDB or .FIT-to-Open-mHealth conversions on which the release depends.

No file-level checksums or fixity information, no errata slot, and no machine-actionable derivation relations (was_derived_from, parent_datasets) despite the equivalent information being present in prose.

Bias types carry no AIO or CROISSANT RAI ontology identifiers, selection_bias has no mitigation strategy, and the balanced-cohort claim cannot be verified by public reusers because the balancing variables are withheld.
recommendations: Correct the PI affiliation and accountable organization to the University of Washington (ROR:00cvxb145), or state explicitly that the FAIRhub string is a suspected upstream registry error retained verbatim rather than an asserted value.

Assert one operative de-identification method for the public release - Safe Harbor removal of PHI plus removal of sex, race/ethnicity and medications - and demote the FAIRhub 'NoDeIdentification' flag to a source note.

Conduct and record a data protection impact analysis covering re-identification potential in retinal imaging, ECG waveforms and ten-day continuous glucose and activity traces, which PHI removal does not address.

Publish a preservation commitment with a horizon beyond the grant period, a tombstone or retrieval-on-request policy for withdrawn versions such as 2.0.0, and a statement of what the repository review notice implies for continuity.

Name the conversion pipelines with versions and repository URLs under the existing github.com/AI-READI organization, so that .fda/.sdt-to-DICOM, XML-to-WFDB and .FIT-to-Open-mHealth conversions are reproducible from the datasheet.

Populate parent_datasets, regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level ('HL7:2N (normal)'), an errata slot summarising CHANGELOG entries, and file-level checksums, all of which have prose or external equivalents today.

Attach AIO or CROISSANT RAI identifiers to the three bias types, add a measurement or device bias entry for the documented between-device variation across the seven imaging systems, and supply a mitigation strategy for selection_bias.
Mark each subpopulation object as released or controlled-access-only so reusers can tell which demographic variables are actually present in the downloadable files.
